title: Slimline CPU-GPU bridge and lightweight prefill/decoder scheduler
creator: Ayesha Patel
description: Goal: Reduce host-side overheads in the CPU->GPU inference pipeline by introducing a slim CPU-GPU bridge and a lightweight scheduler optimized for prefill+decode flows. This ticket covers design, prototype, measurement, and canary rollout of: 1) a thin transfer orchestration layer that coalesces memcpy operations into per-request pinned staging buffers; 2) a per-GPU work-stealing threadpool to avoid global thread contention; 3) a tiny prefill/decoder scheduler that prioritizes latency-critical requests and exposes kernel-selection hints to the runtime. Expected net improvements: lower 95th/99th prefill latency, reduced CPU utilization, fewer small memcpy syscalls, and cleaner CPU-side contention profiles.
acceptance_criteria: 95th-percentile prefill latency reduced by >=20% on our standard Llama-2-13B testfeed (baseline: 120ms prefill)
CPU syscalls for small host->device copies reduced by >=40% in mixed client workload (measured via strace/ebpf walls)
No regression in peak GPU utilization or model quality; end-to-end throughput within ±5% of baseline when batching is aggressive
Canary rollout with runtime flag turned on shows no increase in error rates, and latency SLOs are met for 72h across two regions
tasks: Design slim CPU-GPU bridge API and memory lifecycle (staged pinned buffers + reuse pool)
Implement per-GPU work-stealing threadpool with local queues and bounded stealing window
Prototype prefill/decoder scheduler that tags high-priority requests and coalesces copies per-request
Add telemetry: host-side histogram of memcpy sizes, thread contention metrics, syscall rates
Benchmark and compare against baseline across four instance types (A100, H100, RTX6000, V100) and synthetic traffic profiles
Write rollout plan and automated canary dashboard checks
Ship behind runtime feature flag and run 72h canary in us-west-2 and eu-west-1
progress_comments: 2026-02-10 — Ayesha Patel: Kickoff meeting held. Identified three levers: copy coalescing, threadpool locality, and lightweight scheduler. Agreed to prioritize minimal API surface so Dedicated/Private customers can opt-in.

2026-02-12 — Liam Chen: PoC for pooled pinned buffers completed. Early microbenchmarks show 30% fewer memcpy syscalls for 512B-8KB transfers. Need to validate memory pressure under 200 concurrent inflights.
2026-02-15 — Sofia Marin (review): Raised concern about pinned memory exhaustion on multi-tenant hosts. Suggested an LRU eviction and soft quota per tenant. Added task to add eviction and telemetry.

2026-02-17 — Liam Chen: Implemented per-GPU local queue + bounded work stealing. Synthetic load shows 2.1x reduction in pthread mutex contention in host orchestrator. Observed slight tail increases when GC-style eviction triggers.

2026-02-19 — Performance lab: Ran full-model runs on H100. Prefill 95th went from 118ms -> 88ms in mixed small/latency workload. Need to test with large-batch throughput profile to ensure no regressions.
2026-02-21 — Ops note: Driver surface area: need CUDA >= 12.2 pinned memory allocator behavior for safe reuse. Blocker documented; coordinating with infra to validate driver versions across clusters.
notes: Trade-offs considered: aggressive zero-copy attempts require cross-process pinning (complex) vs staged pinned buffers which are simpler but use more host memory. We chose staged pinned pool with eviction to limit blast radius.
Kernel-selection hints: scheduler will pass small-sequence hints so runtime prefers faster attention kernels for short sequences. This is advisory only and can be toggled per-model.
Multi-tenant safety: added soft quotas and tenant-scoped buffer accounting to prevent noisy neighbors from exhausting pinned pool.
Rollout strategy: feature flag default off. Start with 5% traffic canary in two regions, then 25%, then 100% if telemetry stable. Automated rollback on SLO breach.
